Baking.question: The _____ was Food-producing method.
Baking.fact: Baking is a method of preparing food or clay that uses dry heat, typically in an oven, hot ashes, or on hot stones.

Baklava.subject: Food Processing
Baklava.question: The _____ was Layered filo pastry dessert.
Baklava.fact: Baklava ( , or ) is a layered pastry dessert made of filo pastry, filled with chopped nuts, and sweetened with either syrup or honey. The name baklava is used in many languages with minor phonetic and spelling variations.

Baklava.subject: Food Processing
Baklava.question: The lexicographer Sevan Nişanyan considers its oldest known forms (pre-_____) to be baklağı and baklağu, and labels it as being of Proto-Turkic origin
Baklava.fact: The lexicographer Sevan Nişanyan considers its oldest known forms (pre-1500) to be baklağı and baklağu, and labels it as being of Proto-Turkic origin.

Bakpia.subject: Food Processing
Bakpia.question: The _____ was Filipino/Indonesian bean-filled moon cake-like pastry.
Bakpia.fact: 'good pastry' - the name it is known by in the Philippines) pia or bakpia (Javanese: ꦧꦏ꧀ꦥꦶꦪ, romanized: bakpia; Chinese: 肉餅; Pe̍h-ōe-jī: bah-piáⁿ; lit. In Indonesia, it is also widely called bakpia pathok, named after a suburb of Yogyakarta which specialises in the pastry.

Bakpia pathok.subject: Food Processing
Bakpia pathok.question: The _____ was Indonesian sweet roll.
Bakpia pathok.fact: Bakpia pathok (Javanese: ꦧꦏ꧀ꦥꦶꦪꦥꦛꦸꦏ꧀, romanized: bakpia pathuk) is a small, round-shaped Chinese-influenced Indonesian sweet roll (bakpia), usually stuffed with mung beans, but have recently come in other fillings as well, such as chocolate, durian and cheese. Bakpia pathok is similar to the larger Indonesian pia, with the only difference being the size.

Banitsa.subject: Food Processing
Banitsa.question: The _____ was Southeastern European pie.
Banitsa.fact: Banitsa (Bulgarian: баница), also transliterated as banica and banitza, is a traditional pie made in Bulgaria. Banitsa is prepared by layering a mixture of whisked eggs, plain yogurt, and pieces of white brined cheese between filo pastry and then baking it in an oven.

Bark bread.subject: Food Processing
Bark bread.question: The _____ was Scandinavian bread used as famine food.
Bark bread.fact: Bark bread is a traditional food made with the inner bark (phloem) of certain trees and shrubs. Bark bread is mentioned in medieval literature, and it may have an even older tradition among the Sami people, with the oldest findings of bark harvests being around 3000 years old.

Bark bread.subject: Food Processing
Bark bread.question: In _____, samples of "emergency bread" were sent from Kristiansand, Norway, to the Royal Administration in Copenhagen, including bark bread, bread made from grainless husks and bread made from burned
Bark bread.fact: In 1742, samples of "emergency bread" were sent from Kristiansand, Norway, to the Royal Administration in Copenhagen, including bark bread, bread made from grainless husks and bread made from burned bones.

Aging (food).subject: Food Processing
Aging (food).question: The _____ was Food preparation process.
Aging (food).fact: Aging or ageing, in the context of food or beverages, is the leaving of a product over an extended period of time (often months or years) to aid in improving the flavor of the product. Aging can be done under a number of conditions, and for a number of reasons including stronger umami flavors and tenderness.

American Institute for Cancer Research.subject: Food Processing
American Institute for Cancer Research.question: The _____ was American non-profit organization.
American Institute for Cancer Research.fact: The American Institute for Cancer Research (AICR) is a large American cancer research organization associated with the World Cancer Research Fund umbrella organization.

American Institute for Cancer Research.subject: Food Processing
American Institute for Cancer Research.question: As of _____, the charity has a four-star rating from Charity Navigator, with a score of 96 out of 100
American Institute for Cancer Research.fact: As of 2024, the charity has a four-star rating from Charity Navigator, with a score of 96 out of 100.

Aspic.subject: Food Processing
Aspic.question: The _____ was Savoury jelly dish.
Aspic.fact: Aspic () or meat jelly is a savoury gelatin made with a meat stock or broth, set in a mold to encase other ingredients. Aspic is also sometimes called aspic gelée or aspic jelly.

Aspic.subject: Food Processing
Aspic.question: A detailed recipe for aspic is found in Le Viandier, written around _____
Aspic.fact: A detailed recipe for aspic is found in Le Viandier, written around 1375.

Bacon.subject: Food Processing
Bacon.question: The _____ was Type of salt-cured pork.
Bacon.fact: Bacon is a type of salt-cured pork made from various cuts, typically the belly or less fatty parts of the back. Bacon is also used for barding and larding roasts, especially game, including venison and pheasant, and may also be used to insulate or flavour roast joints by being layered onto the meat.

Bain-marie.subject: Food Processing
Bain-marie.question: The _____ was Device for double boiling, often used for cooking and material creation.
Bain-marie.fact: A bain-marie (English: BAN-mə-REE, French: [bɛ̃ maʁi]), also called a water bath or double boiler, a type of heated bath, is a piece of equipment used in science, industry, and cooking to heat materials gently or to keep materials warm over a period of time. A bain-marie is also used to melt ingredients for cooking.

Barrel.subject: Food Processing
Barrel.question: The _____ was Hollow cylindrical container.
Barrel.fact: A barrel or cask is a hollow cylindrical container with a bulging center, longer than it is wide. The word vat is often used for large containers for liquids, usually alcoholic beverages; a small barrel or cask is called a keg.

Barbecue.subject: Food Processing
Barbecue.question: The _____ was Cooking method and apparatus.
Barbecue.fact: Barbecue or barbeque (often shortened to BBQ worldwide; barbie or barby in Australia and New Zealand) is a term used with regional and national variations to describe various cooking methods, employing live fire and smoke to cook food. The various regional variations of barbecue can be categorized into methods using direct or indirect heating.

Basting (cooking).subject: Food Processing
Basting (cooking).question: The _____ was Periodically coating cooking meat with sauces.
Basting (cooking).fact: Basting is a cooking technique that involves cooking meat with either its own juices or some type of preparation such as a sauce or marinade, such as barbecue. The meat is left to cook, then periodically coated with the juice.

Biltong.subject: Food Processing
Biltong.question: The _____ was Southern African air-dried cured meat.
Biltong.fact: Biltong is a form of air-dried, cured meat which originated in Southern Africa.

Blackening (cooking).subject: Food Processing
Blackening (cooking).question: The _____ was Method to form a crust of herbs and spices.
Blackening (cooking).fact: Blackening is a cooking technique used in the preparation of fish and other foods. Often associated with Cajun cuisine, this technique was invented and popularized by chef Paul Prudhomme.

Blanching (cooking).subject: Food Processing
Blanching (cooking).question: The _____ was Brief scalding of food in boiling water.
Blanching (cooking).fact: Blanching is a process in which a food, usually a vegetable or fruit, is partially cooked by first scalding in boiling water, then removing after a brief timed interval, and finally plunging into iced water or placing under cold running water (known as shocking or refreshing) to halt the cooking process. Blanching foods helps reduce quality loss over time.

Boiling.subject: Food Processing
Boiling.question: The _____ was Physical process.
Boiling.fact: Boiling or ebullition is the rapid phase transition from liquid to gas or vapour; the reverse of boiling is condensation. Boiling occurs when a liquid is heated to its boiling point, so that the vapour pressure of the liquid is equal to the pressure exerted on the liquid by the surrounding atmosphere.

Bracken.subject: Food Processing
Bracken.question: The _____ was Genus of ferns.
Bracken.fact: Bracken (Pteridium) is a genus of large, cosmopolitan, coarse ferns in the family Dennstaedtiaceae. Brackens are noted for their large, highly divided fronds and are found on all continents except Antarctica; their typical habitat is moorland.

Braising.subject: Food Processing
Braising.question: The _____ was Combination-cooking method using wet and dry heat.
Braising.fact: Braising (from the French word braiser) is a combination cooking method that uses both wet and dry heats: typically, the food is first browned at a high temperature, then simmered in a covered pot in cooking liquid (such as wine, broth, coconut milk, or beer). It is similar to stewing, but braising is done with less liquid and usually used for larger cuts of meat.

Brine.subject: Food Processing
Brine.question: The _____ was Concentrated solution of salt in water.
Brine.fact: Brine (or briny water) is a high-concentration solution of salt (typically sodium chloride or calcium chloride) in water. In diverse contexts, brine may refer to the salt solutions ranging from about 3.5% (a typical concentration of seawater, on the lower end of that of solutions used for brining foods) up to about 26% (a typical saturated solution, depending on temperature).

Brining.subject: Food Processing
Brining.question: The _____ was Food processing by treating with brine or salt.
Brining.fact: Brining is treating food with brine or coarse salt which preserves and seasons the food while enhancing tenderness. Brining is similar to marination, except that a marinade usually includes a significant amount of acid, such as vinegar or citrus juice.

Caramelization.subject: Food Processing
Caramelization.question: The _____ was Process of browning of sugar.
Caramelization.fact: Caramelization is a process of browning of sugar used extensively in cooking for the resulting butter-like flavor and brown color. Like the Maillard reaction, caramelization is a type of non-enzymatic browning.

Cardiovascular disease.subject: Food Processing
Cardiovascular disease.question: The _____ was Disease involving heart or blood vessels.
Cardiovascular disease.fact: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is any disease involving the heart or blood vessels.

Acid–base disorder.subject: Food Processing
Acid–base disorder.question: The _____ was Abnormality of the human body's normal balance of acids and bases.
Acid–base disorder.fact: Acid–base imbalance is an abnormality of the human body's normal balance of acids and bases that causes the plasma pH to deviate out of the normal range (7.35 to 7.45). In the fetus, the normal range differs based on which umbilical vessel is sampled (umbilical vein pH is normally 7.25 to 7.45; umbilical artery pH is normally 7.18 to 7.38).

Acid–base disorder.subject: Food Processing
Acid–base disorder.question: The quantitative approach introduced by Peter A Stewart in _____ is newer
Acid–base disorder.fact: The quantitative approach introduced by Peter A Stewart in 1978 is newer.

Appetite.subject: Food Processing
Appetite.question: The _____ was Desire to eat food.
Appetite.fact: Appetite is the desire to eat food items, usually due to hunger. Appealing foods can stimulate appetite even when hunger is absent, although appetite can be greatly reduced by satiety.

Aquaporin.subject: Food Processing
Aquaporin.question: The _____ was Water channel protein in cell membranes.
Aquaporin.fact: Aquaporins, also called water channels, are channel proteins from a larger family of major intrinsic proteins that form pores in the membrane of biological cells, mainly facilitating transport of water between cells. The cell membranes of a variety of different bacteria, fungi, animal and plant cells contain aquaporins.

Aquaporin.subject: Food Processing
Aquaporin.question: The _____ Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded jointly to Peter Agre for the discovery of aquaporins and Roderick MacKinnon for his work on the structure and mechanism of potassium channels
Aquaporin.fact: The 2003 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded jointly to Peter Agre for the discovery of aquaporins and Roderick MacKinnon for his work on the structure and mechanism of potassium channels.

Blood urea nitrogen.subject: Food Processing
Blood urea nitrogen.question: The _____ was Blood test.
Blood urea nitrogen.fact: Blood urea nitrogen (BUN) is a medical test that measures the amount of urea nitrogen found in blood.

Blood volume.subject: Food Processing
Blood volume.question: The _____ was Volume of blood in an organism's circulatory system.
Blood volume.fact: Blood volume (volemia) is the volume of blood (blood cells and plasma) in the circulatory system of any individual. Blood volume (BV) can be calculated given the hematocrit (HC; the fraction of blood that is red blood cells) and plasma volume (PV), with the hematocrit being regulated via the blood oxygen content regulator: B V = P V 1 − H C {\displaystyle BV={\frac {PV}{1-HC}}} Blood volume measurement may be used in people with congestive heart failure, chronic hypertension, kidney failure a...

Blood volume.subject: Food Processing
Blood volume.question: Total Blood Volume has been measured manually by the use of carbon monoxide (CO) as a tracer for more than 100 years and was first proposed by French scientists Grehant and Quinquaud in _____
Blood volume.fact: Total Blood Volume has been measured manually by the use of carbon monoxide (CO) as a tracer for more than 100 years and was first proposed by French scientists Grehant and Quinquaud in 1882.

Blood volume.subject: Food Processing
Blood volume.question: Soon after a usable set-up for human use was developed by Oxford scientists John Haldane and Lorrain Smith and presented in the Journal of Physiology in _____
Blood volume.fact: Soon after a usable set-up for human use was developed by Oxford scientists John Haldane and Lorrain Smith and presented in the Journal of Physiology in 1900.

Body water.subject: Food Processing
Body water.question: The _____ was Water content of an animal's body.
Body water.fact: In physiology, body water is the water content of an animal body that is contained in the tissues, the blood, the bones and elsewhere. The percentages of body water contained in various fluid compartments add up to total body water (TBW).

Cause (medicine).subject: Food Processing
Cause (medicine).question: The _____ was Reason for or origin of a disease or pathology.
Cause (medicine).fact: Cause, also called etiology () or aetiology, is the reason or origination of something. The word etiology is derived from the Greek αἰτιολογία (aitiología), meaning "giving a reason for" (from Ancient Greek αἰτία (aitía) 'cause' and -λογία (-logía)).

Chronic kidney disease.subject: Food Processing
Chronic kidney disease.question: The _____ was Abnormal kidney structure or gradual loss of kidney function.
Chronic kidney disease.fact: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a type of long-term kidney disease, defined by the sustained presence of abnormal kidney function and/or abnormal kidney structure.

Coma.subject: Food Processing
Coma.question: The _____ was State of unconsciousness.
Coma.fact: A coma (from Ancient Greek κῶμα koma 'deep sleep') is a prolonged state of deep unconsciousness in which a person cannot be awakened, fails to respond normally to stimuli (including pain, light, and sound), lacks a normal sleep-wake cycle and does not initiate voluntary actions. People in a coma often require extensive medical care to maintain their health and prevent complications such as pneumonia or blood clots.

3D printing filament.subject: Food Processing
3D printing filament.question: The _____ was Thermoplastic feedstock for 3D printers.
3D printing filament.fact: 3D printing filament is the thermoplastic feedstock for fused filament fabrication 3D printers.

Anodizing.subject: Food Processing
Anodizing.question: The _____ was Metal treatment process.
Anodizing.fact: Anodizing is an electrolytic passivation process used to increase the thickness of the natural oxide layer on the surface of metal parts. The process is called anodizing because the part to be treated forms the anode electrode of an electrolytic cell.

Baby food.subject: Food Processing
Baby food.question: The _____ was Food made especially for infants.
Baby food.fact: Baby food is any soft, easily consumed food other than breastmilk or infant formula that is made specifically for human babies between six months and two years old. In Italy in 2020, a survey of parents found that more than two-thirds of babies were first fed baby food when they were five or six months old.

Baby food.subject: Food Processing
Baby food.question: In Italy in _____, a survey of parents found that more than two-thirds of babies were first fed baby food when they were five or six months old
Baby food.fact: In Italy in 2020, a survey of parents found that more than two-thirds of babies were first fed baby food when they were five or six months old.

Baby food.subject: Food Processing
Baby food.question: A survey in Scotland in _____ indicated that almost no babies were fed baby food before the age of four months, and that about half of them were not given baby food until they were at least six months
Baby food.fact: A survey in Scotland in 2017 indicated that almost no babies were fed baby food before the age of four months, and that about half of them were not given baby food until they were at least six months old.

Biomass briquettes.subject: Food Processing
Biomass briquettes.question: The _____ was Fuel source made from green waste.
Biomass briquettes.fact: Biomass briquettes are a biofuel substitute made of biodegradable green waste with lower emissions of greenhouses gases and carbon dioxide than traditional fuel sources. Biomass briquettes have become popular in developed countries due to the accessibility, and eco-friendly impact.

Brass.subject: Food Processing
Brass.question: The _____ was Alloy of copper and zinc.
Brass.fact: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc, in proportions which can be varied to achieve different colours and mechanical, electrical, acoustic, and chemical properties, but copper typically has the larger proportion, generally 2⁄3 copper and 1⁄3 zinc. Brass is similar to bronze, a copper alloy that contains tin instead of zinc.

Brazing.subject: Food Processing
Brazing.question: The _____ was Metal-joining technique.
Brazing.fact: Brazing is a metal-joining process in which two or more metal items are joined by melting a filler metal which flows into the joint, with the filler metal having a lower melting point than the adjoining metal. During the brazing process, the filler metal flows into the gap between close-fitting parts by capillary action.

Breakfast cereal.subject: Food Processing
Breakfast cereal.question: The _____ was Processed food made from grain.
Breakfast cereal.fact: Breakfast cereal is a category of food, including food products, made from processed cereal grains, that are eaten as part of breakfast or as a snack food, primarily in Western societies.

Briquette.subject: Food Processing
Briquette.question: The _____ was Compressed block of biomass used for fueling a fire.
Briquette.fact: A briquette (French: [bʁikɛt]; in English also spelled briquet or brickette) is a compressed block of coal dust or other combustible biomass material (e.g.

Casting.subject: Food Processing
Casting.question: The _____ was Manufacturing process in which a liquid is poured into a mold to solidify.
Casting.fact: Casting is a manufacturing process in which a liquid material is usually poured into a mold, which contains a hollow cavity of the desired shape, and then allowed to solidify. The solidified part is also called a casting, which is ejected or broken out of the mold to complete the process.

Castor oil.subject: Food Processing
Castor oil.question: The _____ was Vegetable oil pressed from castor beans.
Castor oil.fact: Castor oil is a vegetable oil pressed from castor beans, the seeds of the plant Ricinus communis.

Castor oil.subject: Food Processing
Castor oil.question: _____ BC Ebers Papyrus, and it was in use several centuries earlier
Castor oil.fact: 1550 BC Ebers Papyrus, and it was in use several centuries earlier.

Charles's law.subject: Food Processing
Charles's law.question: The _____ was Relationship between volume and temperature of a gas at constant pressure.
Charles's law.fact: Charles's law (also called the law of volumes) is an experimental gas law that describes how gases tend to expand when heated. A modern statement of Charles's law is: When the pressure on a sample of a dry gas is held constant, the Kelvin temperature and the volume will be in direct proportion.

Charles's law.subject: Food Processing
Charles's law.question: In two of a series of four essays presented between 2 and 30 October _____, John Dalton demonstrated by experiment that all the gases and vapours that he studied expanded by the same amount between tw
Charles's law.fact: In two of a series of four essays presented between 2 and 30 October 1801, John Dalton demonstrated by experiment that all the gases and vapours that he studied expanded by the same amount between two fixed points of temperature.

Charles's law.subject: Food Processing
Charles's law.question: The French natural philosopher Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac confirmed the discovery in a presentation to the French National Institute on 31 Jan _____, although he credited the discovery to unpublished wor
Charles's law.fact: The French natural philosopher Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac confirmed the discovery in a presentation to the French National Institute on 31 Jan 1802, although he credited the discovery to unpublished work from the 1780s by Jacques Charles.

Chromatography.subject: Food Processing
Chromatography.question: The _____ was Set of laboratory techniques for separation of mixtures.
Chromatography.fact: In chemical analysis, chromatography is a laboratory technique for the separation of a mixture into its components.

Apparent molar property.subject: Food Processing
Apparent molar property.question: The _____ was Difference in properties of one mole of substance in a mixture vs. an ideal solution.
Apparent molar property.fact: In thermodynamics, an apparent molar property of a solution component in a mixture or solution is a quantity defined with the purpose of isolating the contribution of each component to the non-ideality of the mixture.

Amphiphile.subject: Food Processing
Amphiphile.question: The _____ was Chemical compound with both hydrophilic and lipophilic properties.
Amphiphile.fact: In chemistry, an amphiphile (from Greek αμφις (amphis) 'both' and φιλíα (philia) 'love, friendship'), also called an amphipath, is a dipolar chemical compound possessing both hydrophilic (water-loving, polar) and lipophilic (fat-loving, nonpolar) properties within the same molecule.

Bilirubin.subject: Food Processing
Bilirubin.question: The _____ was Red pigment of the bile.
Bilirubin.fact: Bilirubin (BR) (adopted from German, originally bili, for bile, plus ruber, Latin for red) is a red-orange compound that occurs as the reduction product of biliverdin, a breakdown product of heme. Although bilirubin is usually found in animals rather than plants, at least one plant species, Strelitzia nicolai, is known to contain the pigment.

Buffer solution.subject: Food Processing
Buffer solution.question: The _____ was Aqueous solution of a weak acid and its conjugate base.
Buffer solution.fact: A buffer solution is a solution where the pH does not change significantly on dilution or if an acid or base is added at constant temperature. Buffer solutions are used as a means of keeping pH at a nearly constant value in a wide variety of chemical applications.

Chemical polarity.subject: Food Processing
Chemical polarity.question: The _____ was Separation of electric charge in a molecule.
Chemical polarity.fact: In chemistry, polarity is a separation of electric charge leading to a molecule or its chemical groups having an electric dipole moment, with a negatively charged end and a positively charged end. Polar molecules must contain one or more polar bonds due to a difference in electronegativity between the bonded atoms.

Colloid.subject: Food Processing
Colloid.question: The _____ was Mixture of an insoluble substance microscopically dispersed throughout another substance.
Colloid.fact: A colloid is a mixture in which one substance, consisting of microscopically dispersed insoluble particles, is suspended throughout another substance. A colloid has a dispersed phase (the suspended particles) and a continuous phase (the medium of suspension).

Colloid.subject: Food Processing
Colloid.question: This field of study began in _____ with Francesco Selmi, who called them pseudosolutions, and was later expanded by Michael Faraday and Thomas Graham, who coined the term colloid in 1861
Colloid.fact: This field of study began in 1845 with Francesco Selmi, who called them pseudosolutions, and was later expanded by Michael Faraday and Thomas Graham, who coined the term colloid in 1861.

Dilution (equation).subject: Food Processing
Dilution (equation).question: The _____ was Chemistry concept.
Dilution (equation).fact: Dilution is the process of decreasing the concentration of a solute in a solution, usually simply by mixing with more solvent like adding more water to the solution. To dilute a solution means to add more solvent without the addition of more solute.

Dilution ratio.subject: Food Processing
Dilution ratio.question: The _____ was Change in concentration when mixing two liquids.
Dilution ratio.fact: In chemistry and biology, the dilution ratio and dilution factor are two related (but slightly different) expressions of the change in concentration of a liquid substance when mixing it with another liquid substance. For example, in a solution with a 1:5 dilution ratio, entails combining 1 unit volume of solute (the material to be diluted) with 5 unit volumes of the solvent to give 6 total units of total volume.

Enthalpy change of solution.subject: Food Processing
Enthalpy change of solution.question: The _____ was Change in enthalpy from dissolving a substance.
Enthalpy change of solution.fact: In thermochemistry, the enthalpy of solution (heat of solution or enthalpy of solvation) is the enthalpy change associated with the dissolution of a substance in a solvent at constant pressure resulting in infinite dilution. The enthalpy of solution is most often expressed in kJ/mol at constant temperature.

Equivalent concentration.subject: Food Processing
Equivalent concentration.question: The _____ was Molar concentration divided by equivalence factor.
Equivalent concentration.fact: In chemistry, equivalent concentration or normality (N) is the number of equivalence of solute (eq) per liter of solution (L).

Eutectic system.subject: Food Processing
Eutectic system.question: The _____ was Mixture with a lower melting point than its constituents.
Eutectic system.fact: A eutectic system or eutectic mixture ( yoo-TEK-tik) is a type of a homogeneous mixture that has a melting point lower than those of the constituents.

Eutectic system.subject: Food Processing
Eutectic system.question: The term eutectic was coined in _____ by the British physicist and chemist Frederick Guthrie (1833–1886)
Eutectic system.fact: The term eutectic was coined in 1884 by the British physicist and chemist Frederick Guthrie (1833–1886).

Flory–Huggins solution theory.subject: Food Processing
Flory–Huggins solution theory.question: The _____ was Lattice model of polymer solutions.
Flory–Huggins solution theory.fact: Flory–Huggins solution theory is a lattice model of the thermodynamics of polymer solutions which takes account of the great dissimilarity in molecular sizes in adapting the usual expression for the entropy of mixing.

Flory–Huggins solution theory.subject: Food Processing
Flory–Huggins solution theory.question: The theory is named after Paul Flory  and Maurice Loyal Huggins  who developed it independently in _____
Flory–Huggins solution theory.fact: The theory is named after Paul Flory  and Maurice Loyal Huggins  who developed it independently in 1941.

Henry's law.subject: Food Processing
Henry's law.question: The _____ was Gas law regarding proportionality of dissolved gas.
Henry's law.fact: In physical chemistry, Henry's law is a gas law that states that the amount of dissolved gas in a liquid is directly proportional at equilibrium to its partial pressure above the liquid. The proportionality factor is called Henry's law constant.

Hydrophile.subject: Food Processing
Hydrophile.question: The _____ was Molecular entity that is attracted to water.
Hydrophile.fact: A hydrophile is a molecule or other molecular entity that is attracted to water molecules and tends to be dissolved by water.

Hydrophobe.subject: Food Processing
Hydrophobe.question: The _____ was Molecule or surface that has no attraction to water.
Hydrophobe.fact: In chemistry, hydrophobicity is the chemical property of a molecule (called a hydrophobe) that is seemingly repelled from a mass of water. Because water molecules are polar, hydrophobes do not dissolve well among them.

Ideal solution.subject: Food Processing
Ideal solution.question: The _____ was Solution exhibiting thermodynamic properties analogous to an ideal gas.
Ideal solution.fact: An ideal solution or ideal mixture is a solution that exhibits thermodynamic properties analogous to those of a mixture of ideal gases. The concept of an ideal solution is fundamental to both thermodynamics and chemical thermodynamics and their applications, such as the explanation of colligative properties.

Aldicarb.subject: Food Processing
Aldicarb.question: The _____ was Chemical compound (insecticide).
Aldicarb.fact: Aldicarb is a carbamate insecticide which is the active substance in the pesticide Temik. Aldicarb is a cholinesterase inhibitor which prevents the breakdown of acetylcholine in the synapse.

Aldicarb.subject: Food Processing
Aldicarb.question: Aldicarb was first synthesized in _____ by Payne and Weiden, and was sold on the market for the first time in 1970
Aldicarb.fact: Aldicarb was first synthesized in 1965 by Payne and Weiden, and was sold on the market for the first time in 1970.

Amoebiasis.subject: Food Processing
Amoebiasis.question: The _____ was Human disease caused by amoeba protists.
Amoebiasis.fact: Amoebiasis, or amoebic dysentery, is an infection of the intestines caused by a parasitic amoeba Entamoeba histolytica. Amoebiasis can be present with no, mild, or severe symptoms.

Antibiotic use in livestock.subject: Food Processing
Antibiotic use in livestock.question: The _____ was Use of antibiotics for any purpose in the husbandry of livestock.
Antibiotic use in livestock.fact: The use of antibiotics in the husbandry of livestock includes treatment when ill (therapeutic), treatment of a group of animals when at least one is diagnosed with clinical infection (metaphylaxis), and preventative treatment (prophylaxis). Antibiotics are an important tool to treat animal as well as human disease, safeguard animal health and welfare, and support food safety.

Antibiotic use in livestock.subject: Food Processing
Antibiotic use in livestock.question: Furthermore, a _____ study also estimates that global agricultural antibiotic usage will increase by 67% from 2010 to 2030, mainly from increases in use in developing BRIC countries
Antibiotic use in livestock.fact: Furthermore, a 2015 study also estimates that global agricultural antibiotic usage will increase by 67% from 2010 to 2030, mainly from increases in use in developing BRIC countries.

Antibiotic use in livestock.subject: Food Processing
Antibiotic use in livestock.question: In _____, the World Health Organization strongly suggested reducing antibiotic use in animals used in the food industry
Antibiotic use in livestock.fact: In 2017, the World Health Organization strongly suggested reducing antibiotic use in animals used in the food industry. The use of antibiotics for growth promotion purposes was banned in the European Union from 2006, and the use of sub-therapeutic doses of medically important antibiotics in animal feed and water to promote growth and improve feed efficiency became illegal in the United States on 1 January 2017, through regulatory change enacted by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), which...

Alastair Ruadh MacDonnell.subject: Food Processing
Alastair Ruadh MacDonnell.question: The _____ was Scottish spy.
Alastair Ruadh MacDonnell.fact: Alastair Roy MacDonell of Glengarry (ca 1725–1761; Scottish Gaelic: Alasdair Ruadh MacDomhnaill, was the 13th chief of Clan MacDonell of Glengarry. Brought up as a Catholic and largely educated in France, he was arrested in November 1745 on his way to join the 1745 Jacobite Rising.
